scope: 15 caller-stack slots: 12 fixed scratch buffers, recvfrom output length, sendmsg header and control header
findings: Existing vinix_stack_alloc macro expands __builtin_alloca in the calling function; fixed sizes are allocated once outside transfer loops and expire only when that call returns.
Original data/address zero initializers and receive-address0xff sentinel remain; the length and MsgHdr initializers preserve their previous values.
Blocking socket operations keep the calling kernel stack live, and every usercopy completes before syscall return.
UNIX binding copies names into owned fields and namespace entries; connection retains socket objects rather than scratch addresses; send/receive copy bytes into or out of owned rings.
INET TCP uses TCP_WRITE_FLAG_COPY, UDP uses PBUF_RAM and pbuf_take; Netlink copies synchronously.

recvfrom length is written only during synchronous receive/address copy. collect_passed_fds consumes the control header immediately; queued FD groups contain owned FD references, no MsgHdr or scratch pointer.
Existing heap allocation and defers for large messages/control data remain unchanged; no new free or grace-period path.
generated_c: Both architectures verify all15 caller-stack slots. Independent x86 review: selected six transfer functions have11 stack slots and zero memdup; four remaining address-only slots present in bind/connect/name functions.
